title: 대수기하학 원론 (EGA) — 한국어 누적판 / Éléments de géométrie algébrique — Korean Cumulative Edition
description:
Éléments de géométrie algébrique — Korean Cumulative Edition (대수기하학 원론 (EGA) — 한국어 누적판), release 2026-09-07-r61.

The PDF presented first is the current cumulative reader: every Korean EGA passage admitted so far through exact source, translation, typesetting, and deterministic validation gates. It contains complete Korean EGA 0_I and EGA I; the complete EGA II Chapter II programme and table of contents; and uninterrupted EGA II main text through §2.9.5, canonical French source ega2-1-fr.tex lines 1–4040. The reader has 264 A4 pages and preserves 253 historical source-page boundaries. EGA II and the complete EGA corpus remain unfinished. Line 4041 is blank and line 4042 begins Section 3, the next translation frontier; this release makes no corpus-completion claim.

The contiguous R49–R61 increment extends the reader from §2.5.12 through the end of Section 2. It develops tensor and Hom constructions for sheaves associated with graded modules; twists and graded section modules; finite generation; functoriality and base change for Proj; criteria for the induced morphism to be finite or an isomorphism; and closed subschemes defined by homogeneous ideals. Formulae, environments, labels, references, terminology, and historical page markers remain bound to exact French slices and Korean candidate hashes. Later untranslated references use non-linking fallbacks rather than fabricated PDF targets.

The cumulative Korean EGA II target is 181,163 UTF-8 bytes / 4,138 LF characters / SHA-256 893C8E4D68134E0F03479D760F916AADD2DA4687CFF8E04DAA300C355023EF9D. Its admitted French prefix is 173,428 bytes / SHA-256 E6911F259382EBEFA590F25970FD3F47297E1EC78D8C4703AD1627DA0BA4C720. A same-day scan-level EGA I correction was reconciled before compilation: the Korean closure paragraph already expressed the correct object, so only its source-authority binding changed. The PDF is 1,618,555 bytes / SHA-256 ED7DE0C7330DD035CA7389B6435C9C7AB16A815237C0750CD241A235DF80DEC6.

One mutex-held four-pass XeLaTeX cycle converged byte-exactly on passes 3–4. One aggregate whole-reader QA—without small-section or repeated QA loops—checked 17 Korean inputs, 23 canonical driver rows, 1,204 labels, 1,647 source hyperlinks with zero missing targets, 740 PDF destinations, 1,878 link annotations, two full-text extractions with identical 167,356-Hangul counts, embedded fonts, A4 geometry, and 200-dpi renders covering the front, contents, prior frontier, and every new tail page. No observed clipping, overlap, tofu, black box, broken diagram, damaged formula, unreadable text, replacement character, fatal TeX diagnostic, unresolved link, or false completion claim survived.

The stable Korean-edition DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.21921513; the exact r61 DOI is 10.5281/zenodo.22647516. The public repository is github.com/KokunoYumeto/ega-ko. Exact r48 DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22645017 remains immutable history. Editable TeX, the fail-closed coverage matrix, evidence, extracts, renders, sanitized build log, and SHA-256 manifest accompany the reader.

The work is held hard against error, but the evidence proves only what was tested. This independent translation is not a critical edition and claims neither perfection, infallibility, finality, external human certification, nor endorsement. Legacy Type1 mathematics-font extraction is not lossless; editable TeX and rendered formulae remain authoritative. Confirmed errors and uncertainties are corrected in later immutable versions.

Alexander Grothendieck and Jean Dieudonné are the historical creators. AI typesetting & translation is the sole standardized project contributor. The historical authors, NUMDAM, IHÉS, publishers, repositories, and cited third parties do not endorse this independently maintained Korean edition.

CC BY 4.0 applies only where the project holds the relevant rights: the Korean translation and typesetting, plus project-authored metadata, indexes, decisions, and QA evidence. It makes no blanket public-domain or open-license claim for the underlying mathematical work, historical French edition, NUMDAM files, bibliography, or third-party content. Every source retains its exact provenance, attribution, author/source relationship, rights, and licence status.
